title: Microdocs authoring patterns and snippet lab (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight lab + playbook for producing tiny, copy-first docs (microdocs) and a guarded snippet library for SDK quickstarts. Goal is to cut the 10-minute onboarding friction to under 3 minutes for experienced engineers and under 10 minutes for product devs.

Audience:
- Integrators and backend devs looking for a minimal reproducible example
- SDK authors who need copy + snippet templates
- UX writers pairing with engineers to ship ephemeral microcopy

Goals (measurable):
- Create 12 canonical microdocs (Python/Node/Go/minimal HTTP) by end of Q1
- Each microdoc must include a 3-line explainer, a 5-line code snippet that runs in Playgrounds, and a one-click curl equivalent
- Add telemetry hooks in every snippet: SDK-instrumented event + example to send minimal traces
- Reduce first-success time in user testing from 7m -> 3m (bench test)

Constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: full tutorial or deep API reference (those live in repo docs). Microdocs are entry points that link out.
- Keep examples un-opinionated about orchestration; prefer hosted examples with notes on Dedicated/Private deviations.

Microdocs format (opinionated):
1) Title (1 line)
2) One-liner (1 sentence) — what you get in 10s
3) TL;DR 3 steps (1-3 short bullets)
4) Copy-first snippet(s): minimal Python and Node or a single HTTP curl + expected JSON response example (<= 8 lines each)
5) Telemetry: one-liner on what to capture + sample code to emit telemetry event
6) Troubleshooting quick note (2 bullets)
7) Links: SDK reference, Quickstart video, relevant GH/PR/Jira

Example microdoc outline (raw draft):
Title: Send a completion in 3 lines (Python)
One-liner: Generate a short assistant reply from a prompt using the Redwood hosted API.
TL;DR:
- pip install redwood-sdk
- set REDWOOD_API_KEY
- run the snippet below

Python snippet:
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
print(client.generate("Translate to emoji: good morning"))

curl equivalent:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' -d '{"prompt":"Translate to emoji: good morning"}'

Expected output (example):
{"text":"☀️😊"}

Telemetry (tiny):
- Capture: event.name=quickstart.run, sdk.version, latency_ms, status
- Python example: client.telemetry.event("quickstart.run", {"success": True})

Troubleshooting:
- 401: missing/misconfigured REDWOOD_API_KEY
- 429: try the smaller prompt or set batch_size=1 in env var

Snippet library rules (practical ops):
- Keep snippets under 12 lines and 1 imported package (except for native http clients)
- Avoid advanced features (streams, tool-calls) unless we provide a second-level microdoc for streaming
- Include explicit env var names in each snippet (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION optional)
- Add a one-line comment for Dedicated/Private deviations (region, host override)
- Each snippet gets a README header with last_tested date and owner handle

Planned experiments (prioritized):
1) Playable snippets embedded in docs with auto-run (web sandbox) — test A/B: with vs without auto-run
2) Microcopy variants for the one-liner — measure drop-offs in first-run success
3) Telemetry opt-in UX: sample snippet that emits identifiable ephemeral events; measure opt-in rate
4) A CLI "microstart" generator: generates a microdoc for new SDK PRs using templates

Quickstart (30-second, 5-step distilled for landing page):
1) Create API key (console)
2) Install client (pip/npm)
3) Run one-liner snippet (copy/paste)
4) Verify output (expected JSON shown)
5) Add telemetry snippet and open a local ticket if an error occurs (next steps)

Authoring checklist for a microdoc (to go in template):
- [ ] Title fits in 60 chars
- [ ] One-liner explains outcome in plain english
- [ ] Code snippet runs in 60s in sandbox
- [ ] Curl equivalent present and correct
- [ ] Telemetry hook included and documented
- [ ] Troubleshooting covers 2 high-likelihood errors
- [ ] Linked artifacts: repo PR, test-id, owner handle

Telemetry quick checklist for snippets:
- Always call client.telemetry.event("quickstart.run", {"ok": true|false}) on snippet exit
- Emit sdk.name and sdk.version as attributes
- Add optional example to show how to send stack traces for exceptions (1-2 lines)

Testing and automation notes:
- Add a lightweight unit test that runs each snippet in CI against a mocked endpoint (use container image redwood/sandbox:light)
- CI should mark snippet status in a small JSON manifest (last_tested, result) — this is external to the doc, but link to results in microdoc header
- Nightly smoke: run all microdocs against staging for regressions; fail noisy microdocs and roll back exercises

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we allow snippets with dependencies (requests/axios) or prefer builtin http libs only? (tradeoff: readability vs realism)
- How opinionated should example prompts be about content length and format (tokens)?
- Should microdocs be localized later? which ones first? (CLI flow, onboarding)

Immediate next actions (next 2 weeks):
- Pair with Arjun to write 3 canonical microdocs (Python generate, Node chat, curl embeddings) — assigned: Maya + Arjun (due 2025-10-22)
- Add CI harness ticket (JIRA-DEVXP-912) — assigned: Leo (due 2025-10-20)
- Prototype playable snippet embed on docs site (Tech spike) — assigned: Sofia (due 2025-11-05)

Notes to self / rough thoughts (informal):
- Keep microdocs discoverable: show "Start here" on SDK landing page with tiny thumbnails
- Consider "microdoc recipes" for common tasks (summarize, extract, rerank) that combine 2 microdocs into a mini flow
- We should measure time-to-first-success in the new onboarding funnel (instrumented via telemetry event)

Appendix: small snippet templates (copy/paste friendly)
- Node minimal (top-level):
const { Redwood } = require('redwood-sdk')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
client.generate('Short summary: The repo readme')
  .then(r => console.log(r.text))
  .catch(e => { client.telemetry.event('quickstart.run', { ok: false }); console.error(e) })

- Go minimal (http):
// curl-style simple http POST using net/http; show where to set API key

End.

(Working draft — share feedback in #devx-snippets or add inline comments)
